K1.stone_why: Coarse straight facets on every curve make the titles and numbers read clearly as chiselled stone on a classical serif skeleton.
K1.carving_why: Faceting is applied consistently to every glyph with clean straight cuts; the narrow hexagonal 0 still separates from the wider O, though bowls are slightly mechanical.
K1.calm_why: Regular-weight titles stay quiet and steady, and the bold set numbers have presence without shouting.
K1.personality_why: The polygonal bowls give a recognisable inscriptional voice, though it feels uniformly processed rather than hand-cut.

K2.stone_why: Finer, smaller facets suggest carving only when you look closely; at a glance it reads mostly as a smooth serif.
K2.carving_why: Subtle cuts are crisp and coherent across letters and digits, with no broken shapes, but the effect is faint.
K2.calm_why: Very calm and even, while the bold weights still carry presence.
K2.personality_why: A slight hint of character on top of what is mostly a familiar book serif.

K3.stone_why: Smooth, uncarved classical serif; any sense of inscription comes only from the Roman letterforms.
K3.calm_why: Balanced, quiet and well weighted, with good presence in the bold numerals.
K3.personality_why: A competent but generic text serif you would not pick out again.

K4.stone_why: Practically the same coarse faceting as K1, so it reads as hewn stone in the same way.
K4.carving_why: Facets are consistent and clean across the alphabet and digits; 0/O and 3/8 stay distinct.
K4.calm_why: Steady regular titles and confident bold numbers, not aggressive.
K4.personality_why: A distinct faceted voice, slightly mechanical in its regularity.

K5.stone_why: Facets plus slight irregular tilts in S, 3, 8 and 5 make it feel the most like hand-hewn rock.
K5.carving_why: The irregularity is mostly coherent, but some glyphs (lopsided 3 and 8, the skewed S) start to look wobbly rather than deliberately cut.
K5.calm_why: Still composed at regular weight, though the unevenness adds a little restlessness.
K5.personality_why: The rough, chipped look is unmistakable and memorable.

K6.stone_why: A heavy, slab-like faceted weight that reads like a massive carved block or monument lettering.
K6.carving_why: Bold facets are crisp and consistent at large size and the digits stay very legible, though the heaviness fills counters a little.
K6.calm_why: Even the 'regular' titles are near-black and wrap onto two lines, and the body is heavy too, so it leans toward shouting.
K6.personality_why: Strong monumental character, but the weight dominates more than any particular carved detail.

K7.stone_why: Looks the same as K5: irregular faceting that reads strongly as hewn stone.
K7.carving_why: The cuts are coherent overall, but the lopsided digits and tilted S drift toward an unsteady, slightly glitchy look.
K7.calm_why: Calm at regular weight, with mild restlessness from the irregular contours.
K7.personality_why: A distinctive hand-chipped voice you would recognise again.
